```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D

DOC = "PCP-008"
UO = "aex"
UO_TITLE = "Anion Exchange Chromatography (Step 8)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ---------------
PARAMS = {p.key: p for p in CFG.unit_op(UO).parameters}
n_params = len(PARAMS)
n_mv = sum(1 for p in PARAMS.values() if p.study == "multivariate")


def rng(k):
    """Characterization range of one parameter, in natural units."""
    p = PARAMS[k]
    return f"{p.prange[0]:g}–{p.prange[1]:g}"


def sp(k):
    """Set-point of one parameter, in natural units."""
    return f"{PARAMS[k].setpoint:g}"


# Design structure, read from the seeded designs rather than assumed.
scr_f, rsm_f = D.screening_factors(UO), D.rsm_factors(UO)
k_scr, k_rsm = len(scr_f), len(rsm_f)
n_scr, c_scr = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "screening")
n_rsm, c_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "rsm"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
n_ax = 2 * k_rsm
f_rsm = n_rsm - c_rsm - n_ax
n_2fi = k_scr * (k_scr - 1) // 2
n_terms_scr = 1 + k_scr + n_2fi
n_terms_rsm = 1 + k_rsm + k_rsm * (k_rsm - 1) // 2 + k_rsm
df_res_scr, df_pe_scr = n_scr - n_terms_scr, c_scr - 1
df_res_rsm, df_pe_rsm = n_rsm - n_terms_rsm, c_rsm - 1

resps = D.responses(UO)
n_resp = len(resps)

# Acceptance criteria: DS specification for the impurity, back-calculated step floor
# for the two viral-clearance responses (D.acceptance_for does the back-calculation).
acc_hcp = D.acceptance_for(UO, "hcp_out_ng_mg")
acc_xmulv = D.acceptance_for(UO, "xmulv_lrf")
acc_mvm = D.acceptance_for(UO, "mvm_lrf")
mvm_cum = float(cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == "lrv_mvm"].iloc[0]["acc_low"])
n_mc = V["n_monte_carlo"]

# RA-001's initial risk priority numbers for this step, by parameter name.
ra_aex = ra_scope(UO)
rpn = dict(zip(ra_aex["Parameter"], ra_aex["Initial RPN"]))
```

# Purpose and scope

Anion exchange chromatography is the final chromatographic step of the A-Mab drug
substance process, and it is operated in the flow-through mode. This plan defines the
process characterization study for that step, and it is written before the study is
executed, so it states what will be done and how the result will be judged, and it states
no findings.

The study provides the Stage 1 process design record for the anion exchange step under the
lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011], and it supports the transfer of the
drug substance process from the development site to the commercial site (PTP-001). The
ranges justified here are the ranges that will be carried into process performance
qualification.

The plan covers the `{python} n_params` process parameters of the step (@tbl-params), the
quality attributes the step governs (@tbl-cqa), and the qualified scale-down model on
which every study run will be performed. The `{python} n_resp` measured responses are
pool host cell protein, the log reduction factors for XMuLV and for MVM, and step yield.
The work will be executed at development scale and analysed by design of experiments, in
the enhanced development approach described in ICH Q8 and ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11].

The column itself is outside the scope of this plan. Packing, sanitization and resin
life-cycle qualification are covered by SOP-2008 and are not characterized here.
Confirmation of the operating ranges at commercial scale belongs to
Stage 2 and to the process performance qualification, and the cumulative viral clearance
claim for the drug substance is consolidated in PCMR-001, so this plan covers only the
contribution the anion exchange step makes to that claim.

# Objectives

The study is designed to meet the five objectives listed below, and PCR-008 will report
the outcome against each of them in turn.

1. Quantify the effect of load pH, equilibration and wash-1 conductivity, load
   conductivity and protein load on pool host cell protein, on XMuLV and MVM clearance
   and on step yield, over the ranges given in @tbl-params.
2. Define a multivariate operating region in the parameters studied multivariately, within
   which every governed quality attribute meets its acceptance criterion.
3. Establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter and each governed attribute,
   and confirm that the normal operating ranges lie inside those ranges.
4. Classify every parameter of the step under SOP-4001, from the effects the study
   demonstrates and from the risk of operating outside the region.
5. Establish the log reduction the step contributes to the cumulative MVM and XMuLV
   claims, so that the modular clearance argument can be consolidated in PCMR-001
   [@ichq5a].

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The anion exchange step is a flow-through polish. The column is packed with a strong
anion exchange resin and equilibrated at a pH that lies above the isoelectric point of the
acidic process impurities and below that of the antibody. Under those conditions A-Mab
carries a net positive charge and passes through the column. Host cell protein, DNA,
endotoxin and virus particles bind to the resin instead. Product is collected in the
flow-through and in the post-load wash, so the step purifies without a bind and elute
cycle, which is why its yield is high and why its capacity is set by the impurity burden
and not by the product.

Load pH and conductivity govern the separation. Load pH sets the charge on the antibody
and on the impurities, and conductivity sets how strongly the buffer counter-ions compete
with those impurities for the resin surface. As load pH falls the antibody becomes more
positively charged and the acidic impurities less
negatively charged, so binding weakens and clearance falls. As conductivity rises the same
binding is screened and clearance falls again, and the equilibration and wash-1 buffer
acts on this equilibrium at the point where a weakly bound impurity is most likely to be
displaced into the pool, which is why its conductivity is treated as a parameter in its
own right. Protein load sets the mass challenge on the column, and at high load the
impurity burden approaches the binding capacity available to hold it.

The platform is well established. A flow-through anion exchange polish of this design has
been used to manufacture three prior products (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab), and
the mechanism of impurity and virus removal is the same for A-Mab as it is for those
products [@amab2009]. Prior knowledge therefore sets the expectations that this study will
confirm or refute, but it does not by itself define an operating region, because the
ranges, the interactions and the position of the acceptance limits are specific to this
product and this load material.

The mechanistic expectation is specific enough to be tested. Clearance of both model
viruses should fall as load pH falls and as load conductivity rises, and the two factors
should interact, because both act on the same electrostatic equilibrium. Pool host cell
protein should rise with protein load, with equilibration and wash-1 conductivity, and as
load pH falls. Step yield should be high and largely insensitive across the ranges
studied, since the product does not bind to the resin.

## Quality attributes in scope

The quality attributes this step governs are listed in @tbl-cqa, and the two viral safety
attributes carry the highest criticality in that set.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["lrv_mvm", "lrv_xmulv", "hcp", "leached_protein_a", "residual_dna"]))
print()
print(": Quality attributes governed by the anion exchange step, with acceptance criteria "
      "and criticality from the drug substance register. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

The cumulative clearance of MVM is assigned to this step in the drug substance CQA
register. MVM is a non-enveloped parvovirus, so it is not inactivated by the low-pH hold
at Step 6, and the claim rests on the anion exchange step and the small virus retentive
filter together. Those two steps remove virus by different mechanisms, which is what makes their
contributions additive under ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. The step is credited with XMuLV
clearance as well, and there the low-pH hold (PCP-006) carries the larger share while the
filtration step (PCP-009) carries a further increment.

Host cell protein is the impurity attribute that drives the design of this study, and its
criticality is moderate to high (@tbl-cqa). Three steps of the train remove it. Protein A
capture (PCP-005) removes the bulk of the burden, cation exchange (PCP-007) removes most
of the remainder, and this step provides the final reduction before formulation. Residual
DNA and leached Protein A are also reduced here, and the register assigns residual DNA a
very low criticality and leached Protein A a low to moderate one (@tbl-cqa), so neither is
expected to constrain the operating region. Both will be measured at every design point so
that the expectation can be checked.

No claim is made for aggregate removal across the anion exchange step, since aggregate is
polished at cation exchange (PCP-007). The charge variant and glycan distributions are
formed upstream and are not modified by the purification steps themselves [@amab2009], so
they are not responses of this study.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

The pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001 decided which parameters are studied and
how, and its output for this step is reproduced in @tbl-risk. The method is risk ranking
and filtering. A severity score for the potential impact on a quality attribute is
combined with the likelihood of the failure mode and with the ability to detect it, and
the resulting score carries the parameter into a multivariate design, into a univariate
study, or into neither [@ichq9]. Criticality is treated as a continuum and not as a
binary classification [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(ra_scope(UO))
print()
print(": Pre-characterization risk assessment for the anion exchange step, from RA-001. "
      "The assigned study type is the scope this plan inherits. {#tbl-risk}")
```

Load pH, load conductivity and operating flow rate carry the highest score in @tbl-risk.
Load pH and load conductivity score `{python} rpn["Load pH"]`, because a low
load pH reduces both host cell protein removal and viral clearance, and a high load
conductivity reduces clearance in the same way. A loss of viral clearance is scored at the
top of the severity scale. Operating flow rate carries the same score for the same
attribute, but RA-001 assigned it
a univariate study, because it acts on the separation through residence time and not
through the buffer chemistry that sets the binding equilibrium. Equilibration and wash-1
conductivity and protein load score `{python} rpn["Protein load"]`, since their expected
effect is on host cell protein rather than on viral safety.

The `{python} n_mv` parameters assigned to a multivariate study are the factors of the
designed experiments described below, and flow rate is assessed one factor at a time. No
parameter of this step was left unstudied, so the study scope is the whole parameter set
of the unit operation and not a filtered subset of it.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

Every run in this study will be performed on a qualified scale-down model of the
commercial column, and that qualification is what allows the results to be applied to
commercial manufacture (SOP-1001).

The model is designed on the established principles of chromatography scaling. Bed height,
linear velocity, protein load per litre of resin, buffer composition and the volume of
each phase normalized to column volumes are held equal to the commercial values. Column
efficiency is measured before use by plate count and peak asymmetry. A column that fails
the packing criteria of SOP-2008 is repacked before any study run. Residence time at the
model scale therefore matches residence time at commercial scale for the same linear
velocity, which is the property a flow-through separation depends on.

Qualification will compare the model against commercial scale data at set-point
conditions, and replicate runs at the set-point will be compared with the at-scale record
for step yield, pool host cell protein and pool volume. The model will be accepted when the
means do not differ significantly and when every model result falls inside the range
observed at scale. The comparison is documented under SOP-1001. Its completion is a
precondition for starting any characterization run.

Viral clearance cannot be measured at manufacturing scale, because live virus may not be
introduced into a manufacturing facility. The clearance runs will therefore be executed
in a dedicated biosafety laboratory, on a separately qualified small-scale spiking model,
following ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. The virus spike is added to the load at a small volume
fraction, so that the composition of the load is essentially unchanged, and the spiked
load is assayed alongside the pool so that the log reduction factor is the difference
between two measurements from the same run. The qualification of the spiking model, and
not the size of the column, is what supports a clearance claim.

Centre point runs are replicated so that the pure error of the system can be estimated
independently of the fitted model. The screening design carries `{python} c_scr` centre
points and the response-surface design carries `{python} c_rsm`, which give
`{python} df_pe_scr` and `{python} df_pe_rsm` degrees of freedom for pure error. Those
terms are the reference against which lack of fit will be tested.

## Operation

The step will be operated as it is operated at commercial scale, under SOP-2011. The
column is equilibrated with the wash-1 buffer, the load is applied at the target protein
load and linear velocity, the column is washed with the same buffer, and the product is
collected across the flow-through and the wash. Pool collection starts and stops on
ultraviolet absorbance thresholds, and the pool is held refrigerated until it is sampled.

The load material is the cation exchange pool from Step 7. A single pool, or a set of
pools blended to one specification, will be used for the whole study, so that load
composition is not a hidden factor in the design. Before the study starts the load will be
confirmed representative. Protein concentration, pH and conductivity will be adjusted to
the study target, and the acidic charge variant content will be measured by icIEF
(AMV-3013) and confirmed to lie within the range seen in routine cation exchange pools.
The hold time between neutralization of the cation exchange pool and its use as anion
exchange load will be kept within the limit recorded in SOP-2011, because an extended
neutral hold raises the deamidated fraction of the load and changes the charge
distribution that this step has to separate.

Buffers, resin and the column are inputs controlled to platform specification. They are
identity and quality controlled under SOP-2011 and SOP-2008. They are not parameters of
this study, and they are held at their platform values throughout it. Resin lot and column
use history will likewise be held constant across the study, so that the fitted effects
cannot be confounded with resin age.

## Analytical methods

Every response is measured by a validated method, and the validated performance of the
methods that carry the conclusions of this study is given in @tbl-methods.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(method_perf_for(AEX_AMV_REFS, precision_with_unit=True))
print()
print(": Validated performance of the analytical methods that measure the study "
      "responses. {#tbl-methods}")
```

Pool host cell protein is measured by ELISA (AMV-3012). Its intermediate precision is
`{python} f"{amv_3012_precision:g}"`% relative standard deviation, against
`{python} f"{amv_3016_precision:g}"`% for the leached Protein A ELISA (AMV-3016), and
those are the only two methods in @tbl-methods whose precision is reported on a relative
scale. A difference in pool host cell protein therefore has to stand clear of a relative
standard deviation of that size before it can be attributed to a factor of the design.

XMuLV titre is measured by an infectivity assay (AMV-3017) and MVM titre by infectivity
with a molecular confirmation (AMV-3018), while residual DNA is measured by qPCR
(AMV-3014). The precision of the two infectivity assays is reported as a standard
deviation on the log10 scale, which is not comparable with a relative standard deviation.
Both carry an intermediate precision of about
`{python} f"{amv_3018_precision:g}"` log10 (@tbl-methods), so a difference of that order
between two clearance runs sits inside the noise of the assay and will not be interpreted
as an effect of a process parameter.

Step yield is calculated from the product mass in the load and in the pool, each of them
the product of a measured protein concentration and a measured volume, and protein
concentration is measured by ultraviolet absorbance under AMV-3019. Validated performance
for that method, for the charge variant method (AMV-3013) and for the residual DNA method
(AMV-3014) is recorded in the respective method validation reports and is not reproduced
here.

Where the virus titre of a pool falls below the quantitation limit of the infectivity
assay (@tbl-methods), the log reduction factor is a lower bound and will be reported as
such. A lower bound is used as it stands in the modular clearance summary, and it is
never converted into a point estimate.

## Sampling plan

Samples will be taken from the same points in every run, so that the study is balanced in
the analytical dimension as well as in the factors.

Each run of the non-viral designs is sampled at the load and at the pool. The load is
sampled before application for protein concentration, pH, conductivity, host cell protein
and charge variants, and the flow-through pool is sampled after collection for protein
concentration, host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A. A retain of each
pool is stored frozen, so that an unexpected result can be re-tested without repeating
the run.

The viral runs are sampled differently. The spiked load and the flow-through pool are
assayed for infectious virus, and a cytotoxicity and interference control is run for each
matrix, as ICH Q5A(R2) requires [@ichq5a].

Centre point runs are sampled exactly as the factorial runs are. They will be executed at
intervals through the study and not consecutively, so that the pure error term reflects
the variability of the whole campaign and not the variability of a single day.

## Statistical methods

The analysis follows SOP-1002. Each factor is coded so that the midpoint of its
characterization range is zero and the two edges are ±1, and every model is fitted to the
coded factors, so that estimated effects are comparable across factors carrying different
units. Centre point runs sit at the midpoint of every characterization range, which is the
common reference condition of both designs.

The screening study will be analysed with a model carrying every main effect and every
two-factor interaction, fitted by ordinary least squares. An effect is reported as twice
the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response between the two edges of the
studied range. Terms are judged at α = 0.05, and the screening study identifies which
factors and which interactions act on each response. It is not the predictive model, and
no operating range will be defined from it.

The response-surface study will be analysed with the full quadratic model in the
`{python} k_rsm` multivariate factors. That model carries `{python} n_terms_rsm` terms
against `{python} n_rsm` runs and leaves `{python} df_res_rsm` residual degrees of
freedom, and it is the predictive model, so it is the basis of the operating region, of
every proven acceptable range and of the capability estimates in this plan. Model adequacy
will be judged on four statements taken together. These are the significance of the
model F test, the coefficient of determination and its adjusted form, the predicted
coefficient of determination computed from the PRESS residuals, and the lack of fit test
against pure error. Residuals will be inspected against the predicted values, against the
run order and on a normal probability plot.

A factor with no significant effect on any response is a result and not a gap. It will be
classified on the evidence of that absence. It will be retained in the knowledge space as
evidence that the governed attributes are robust to it across the range screened.

Commercial scale capability will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches, with every parameter drawn inside its normal operating
range and the fitted models used to predict each attribute. Capability will be reported as
a one-sided Cpk against the relevant limit. This plan sets no numerical capability
threshold. The report will state each Cpk with the margin between the predicted
distribution and the limit, and the acceptability of that margin will be argued from the
criticality of the attribute and the control capability of the parameters.

# Study design

The design has to separate `{python} k_scr` factors that act on one equilibrium, so the
multivariate work is done in two stages. A screening study identifies the active factors
and interactions, a response-surface study models the region they define, and operating
flow rate is assessed one factor at a time for the mechanistic reason given below.

## Factors, ranges and study type

The parameters, their set-points, the ranges to be studied and the normal operating ranges
are given in @tbl-params, and the coded letters used for the `{python} k_scr` multivariate
factors in the design matrices are given in @tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
print()
print(": Parameters of the anion exchange step, with the ranges to be studied, the normal "
      "operating ranges and the assigned study type. {#tbl-params}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Coded factor legend for the screening and response-surface designs. {#tbl-legend}")
```

Every studied range in @tbl-params is wider than the corresponding normal operating range,
and deliberately so, because a characterization range has to bound the knowledge space,
which means it has to include settings the commercial process will not normally see
[@amab2009]. The wider ranges also support later movement within the operating region
without new studies, and each range was set from prior knowledge and from the mechanism.

Load pH will be studied over `{python} rng("load_ph")` against a set-point of
`{python} sp("load_ph")` (@tbl-params). The lower edge sits below the pH at which prior
products began to lose virus binding, so that the loss of clearance is bounded by
measurement instead of by extrapolation. The upper edge is limited by antibody stability
at the load protein concentration.

Equilibration and wash-1 conductivity will be studied over `{python} rng("wash1_cond")`
mS/cm, where the lower edge is a more dilute buffer than the commercial site will prepare
and the upper edge lies above the conductivity at which platform experience shows host
cell protein beginning to appear in the flow-through.

Load conductivity will be studied over `{python} rng("load_cond")` mS/cm. The load enters
this step from the cation exchange pool, and its conductivity is the input property most
likely to move from batch to batch, so the range is wide enough to cover a cation exchange
pool taken from either end of its own operating region.

Protein load will be studied over `{python} rng("load")` g/L resin, and the upper edge
lies above the highest load the commercial column will be asked to carry, so that the
capacity of the step is bounded by data. The lower edge lies well below the set-point,
because a response-surface model may only be used inside the region it was fitted over,
and the low end of the load range has to be part of that region.

Operating flow rate will be studied over `{python} rng("flow")` cm/hr, one factor at a
time.

## Screening design

The screening study is a two-level full factorial in the `{python} k_scr` multivariate
factors, augmented with `{python} c_scr` centre points, giving `{python} n_scr` runs in
total. The planned matrix is given in Appendix A. A full factorial was chosen in
preference to a fractional design because a design in `{python} k_scr` factors is small
enough to afford it, and because the expected interactions are between factors that act on
the same equilibrium. No
interaction may be aliased with a main effect at this step, since an interaction between
load pH and load conductivity is the effect the viral clearance claim is most sensitive to.

The design estimates all `{python} k_scr` main effects and all `{python} n_2fi` two-factor
interactions independently, and it leaves `{python} df_res_scr` residual degrees of
freedom for the two-factor interaction model. Runs will be executed in a randomized order,
with the centre points distributed through the sequence. The purpose of this study is to
identify which factors and interactions act on each response, and the magnitudes it
estimates will be refined by the response-surface study.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design in the same
`{python} k_rsm` factors, and it carries `{python} f_rsm` factorial runs,
`{python} n_ax` axial runs and `{python} c_rsm` centre points, giving `{python} n_rsm`
runs in total. The planned matrix is given in Appendix B. The axial points sit on the
faces of the cube and not outside it, so no run is executed beyond the characterization
ranges in @tbl-params. That matters here, because those ranges are the edges of the
knowledge space and the study is not permitted to operate the model outside them.

All `{python} k_rsm` multivariate factors are carried into the response-surface design.
None can be excluded in advance, since each is expected to act on at least one of the
`{python} n_resp` responses and the two conductivities are expected to interact with load
pH. The design adds the curvature terms that a two-level screening design cannot estimate.
The fitted quadratic model is the model from which the operating region, the proven
acceptable ranges and the capability estimates will be derived. It is the only model in
this study that will be used to predict.

## Univariate assessment

Operating flow rate will be assessed one factor at a time. It will be run at its
set-point and at each edge of `{python} rng("flow")` cm/hr, with the `{python} k_rsm`
multivariate factors held at their set-points, and the same responses will be measured at
each setting.

The reason it is held out of the multivariate design is mechanistic. Flow rate acts on the
separation through residence time, and residence time governs how closely impurity binding
approaches equilibrium. It does not change the charge state of the antibody or of the
impurities, which is how the multivariate factors act, so an interaction between flow rate
and the solution properties is not expected. RA-001 assigned it a
univariate study on that basis (@tbl-risk). If the univariate runs show an effect on viral
clearance at the high edge of the range, the parameter will be carried into a further
multivariate study and this plan revised under change control.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

This section states the criteria the study must meet, before any data exist. They apply to
the scale-down model, to the fitted models and to the measured quality attributes.

The scale-down model must be qualified before any characterization run starts. The
criterion is the one given above under materials and methods. There must be no significant
difference between the model and the commercial scale record on step yield, pool host cell
protein and pool volume, and every model result must fall inside the range observed at
scale (SOP-1001). Runs performed on a model that has not met that criterion will not be
used to define an operating range.

A fitted model will be used to define the operating region only if it is adequate. The
model F test must be significant at α = 0.05, the lack of fit test against pure error must
not be significant at the same level, and the predicted coefficient of determination must
be close enough to the adjusted value to show that the model predicts and does not merely
fit. A significant lack of fit will be investigated before the model is used, and both the
investigation and its outcome will be reported in PCR-008. Where a response yields no
significant model, that will be reported as an absence of effect over the ranges studied,
and the parameters will be classified on that evidence.

The acceptance criteria for the measured responses are given in @tbl-acceptance, together
with the basis of each.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.acceptance_table(UO))
print()
print(": Acceptance criteria for the measured responses, with the basis of each. "
      "{#tbl-acceptance}")
```

Pool host cell protein is judged against the drug substance specification, which is a
ceiling of `{python} f"{acc_hcp[1]:g}"` ng/mg (@tbl-acceptance). The two viral clearance
responses are judged against a step-level requirement instead, because the specification
is cumulative across the process and no single step is asked to meet it alone. The
cumulative MVM requirement is
`{python} f"{mvm_cum:g}"` log10 (@tbl-cqa), and subtracting the clearance credited to the
other steps of the train leaves `{python} f"{acc_mvm[0]:.2f}"` log10 for this step, while
the same calculation gives `{python} f"{acc_xmulv[0]:.2f}"` log10 for XMuLV. Those two
figures are what the operating region has to satisfy here, and step yield carries no
acceptance criterion at all, since it is measured as a process performance response.

The operating region will be declared acceptable when the fitted response-surface models
predict every governed attribute inside its criterion across the whole region, and when
the normal operating ranges in @tbl-params lie inside it. The worst case corner of the
region follows from the mechanism, and it is the corner at the lowest load pH, the highest
load conductivity, the highest equilibration and wash-1 conductivity and the highest
protein load. Clearance is expected to be lowest there and pool host cell protein highest,
so the region will not be declared acceptable unless the prediction at that corner meets
both criteria.

If a governed attribute fails inside the characterized ranges, the region will be reduced
to the sub-region that meets the criteria, and the boundary will then be reported as an
edge of failure. If that boundary falls inside a normal operating range, the normal
operating range itself will be revised, and the revision will be handled under the
pharmaceutical quality system [@ichq10].

Departures from this plan will be recorded and impact-assessed in PCR-008. A departure
that leaves a run inside its designed setting will be assessed and the run retained. A
departure that makes a run unrepresentative of the commercial process invalidates the
affected design, and a load material outside the acceptance stated above under operation
is such a departure. In that case the affected runs will be repeated in full on
requalified material, and the invalidated data will be retained for the root cause
investigation and excluded from the reported analysis.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

The operating region is multivariate and a proven acceptable range is not. Both will be
reported, and this section states how the ranges will be derived and what they will mean.

The acceptance basis is the one given in @tbl-acceptance. For pool host cell protein the
criterion is the drug substance specification. For the two viral clearance responses it is
the step-level requirement back-calculated from the cumulative requirement, and no other
value is used in this analysis.

Two analyses will be run for each governed attribute and each response-surface factor.
The first holds the other parameters at their set-points and evaluates the fitted
response-surface model across the parameter's characterization range. The second varies
the other parameters inside their normal operating ranges, drawing
`{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"`
Monte-Carlo samples of those parameters at each of `{python} D.PAR_GRID` points across the
range, predicting the attribute from the fitted model with its residual variance included,
and taking the 95% predictive interval of the result.

The decision rule is the same in both analyses. The proven acceptable range is the
contiguous interval of the parameter, containing the set-point, over which the attribute
meets its criterion. In the first analysis that test is applied to the predicted mean, and
in the second it is applied to the whole predictive interval. The second rule is the
stricter of the two, so where the two ranges differ the narrower one is the range the
control strategy will rely on.

Each governed attribute will be reported with a plot of its governing parameter, which is
the parameter carrying the largest main effect on that attribute. The plot carries the
parameter on the horizontal axis and the attribute on the vertical axis, with
the acceptance limit drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and the set-point and the
normal operating range marked. The two analyses appear as the two panels of the same
figure.

The relationship between a proven acceptable range and the operating region has to be
stated, because the two are easily confused. A proven acceptable range is a statement
about one parameter while the others are held or varied in a defined way. The operating
region is a statement about all `{python} k_rsm` factors together. Where a whole
characterization range is proven acceptable for every governed attribute, the binding
constraint on the process is the multivariate corner of the region and not any univariate
range, and the report will say so explicitly.

Every range reported by this method is bounded by the characterization ranges in
@tbl-params and by the fitted model. It says nothing about settings outside those ranges,
and nothing about a load material that falls outside the acceptance stated above under
operation.

# Data management and integrity

Study records will be managed to ALCOA+ expectations. Chromatography runs are recorded by
the instrument control system and analytical results by the laboratory information
management system, and both records are retained with their audit trails for the review
that closes the study. The statistical analysis will be performed in the validated
environment described in SOP-1002, and the analysis scripts and the data extracts are
retained with the study record.

Any value transcribed by hand will be verified by a second person against the source
record. Data excluded from an analysis will be identified in PCR-008 with the reason for
its exclusion, and no result will be removed from the record itself. Raw data, analysis
files and the report are retained for the life of the product.

# Roles and responsibilities

The functions that carry work under this plan are listed in @tbl-roles, and each of them
appears in the approval record at the front of the document as author, reviewer or
approver.

| Function | Responsibility under this plan |
|---|---|
| Process Development / MSAT | Owns this plan, executes the non-viral runs, performs the statistical analysis and writes PCR-008. |
| Analytical Development | Releases the validated methods, analyses the samples and provides the method performance record. |
| Virology laboratory | Executes the spiking runs under ICH Q5A(R2) and reports the titres and log reduction factors. |
| Manufacturing Science | Provides the commercial scale record used to qualify the scale-down model. |
| Statistics | Reviews the designs before execution and the fitted models before they are used. |
| Quality Assurance | Approves this plan, reviews every departure from it and approves PCR-008. |

: Functions and responsibilities under this plan. {#tbl-roles}

The responsibilities in @tbl-roles are assigned to functions and not to individuals, so
the plan does not need revision when staff change.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-008, the process characterization report for the anion
exchange step. It reports the executed designs, the fitted models, the operating region,
the proven acceptable ranges, the estimated capability and the classification of every
parameter, and it records every departure from this plan.

The study runs as a sequence of dependent phases, and the scale-down model is qualified
first. The screening study runs next, and its analysis is completed before the
response-surface study starts, so that the design of the second study can be confirmed
before further runs are committed. The response-surface study follows, while the viral clearance runs are executed in
parallel in the biosafety laboratory, on the same design points, because they use a
different facility and a separate qualification. The univariate flow rate runs may be
executed at any point after the scale-down model is qualified, and analysis and reporting
complete the study.

No calendar dates are given in this plan, since the sequence and the dependencies above
are the schedule, and the executed dates will be recorded in PCR-008.

# Risks and assumptions

The principal risk to this study is that the scale-down model does not represent the
commercial column, and it is managed by the qualification described under materials and
methods, which is the reason no characterization run may start before that qualification
is complete. A residual risk remains after qualification, because the comparison is made
at set-point conditions and representativeness at the edges of the ranges is inferred from
the scaling principles rather than demonstrated. Ranges defined on the model are not
confirmed at commercial scale until Stage 2, and PCR-008 will state that bound on every
range it reports.

The virus spiking model carries assumptions of its own. The model viruses are laboratory
strains chosen as representatives of a class, the spike is added to a load that is not
identical to the commercial load, and the clearance measured is a property of that model
system [@ichq5a]. These assumptions are accepted because the same convention is applied at
every clearance step of this process and was applied to the three prior products, so the
modular claim is at least internally consistent.

Load material supply is a practical risk. The study needs one representative cation
exchange pool, or a set of pools blended to a single specification, and the quantity
required is large in comparison with a development batch. If the load has to be prepared
from more than one cation exchange run, the pools will be blended before any study run and
the blend characterized as described under operation.

The study assumes that the platform mechanism transfers from the three prior products to
A-Mab, which is what makes this a confirmatory study instead of an exploratory one. It
also assumes that the resin lot used in the study represents the resin the commercial
process will use, and that assumption is managed by the resin qualification in SOP-2008.
Both are stated here so that the report can test them, and if either fails the affected
conclusions will be re-derived and not defended.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when it has been approved by each function named in the approval
record at the front of the document. Changes after approval are made by revising the plan
under change control [@ichq10]. A departure identified during execution is not a plan
change. It is recorded and assessed in PCR-008, as described above under acceptance and
decision criteria.
